title: Contextual Surface Paradigm: Layered Sidebar & Route Hints
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: As Redwood Console has grown (dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdowns, per-route observability), users report difficulty locating features and understanding context when switching workspaces. Existing left-rail patterns surface too many static items and force deep navigation for common tasks (canary rollouts, model cost attribution, per-route latency charts). Goal: design an information architecture and navigation pattern that reduces time-to-action for 80% of common workflows (inspect route metrics, start a rollout, view cost breakdown for a model) while preserving discoverability for advanced controls.
proposal_summary: Introduce a layered sidebar that adapts by workspace and primary task, combined with route-hint micronavigation and an immersive quick-preview pane. Key ideas: 1) Workspace-aware primary rail (3–6 persistent sections tuned per workspace role); 2) Contextual secondary rail that surfaces top tasks (Start rollout, View costs, Inspect traces) for the currently selected resource; 3) Route hints — inline pill-style shortcuts inside dashboard headers linking to high-value destinations; 4) Quick-preview flyouts for metrics and cost breakdowns to avoid full context switches; 5) Explicit breadcrumb + escape hatch when deep linking into specific routes to preserve orientation.
usability_findings: Moderate: task completion for 'start canary rollout' improved from 38% to 82% in unmoderated proto test (N=24)
Users prefer inline route-hints in dashboards rather than a global command palette for discoverability
Some confusion around quick-preview persistence — users expected multi-tab previews; added pin affordance
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: favor progressive disclosure over a dense unified nav to reduce cognitive load (means >1 click for rare admin pages)
Tradeoff: quick-preview reduces context switches but complicates keyboard navigation — requires dedicated focus cycle improvements in frontend sprint
Decision: role-aware primary rail configured server-side to allow enterprise tenants to pin controls (adds backend config work)
acceptance_criteria: Layered sidebar implemented with workspace-aware primary rail and contextual secondary rail; visual parity with Figma prototype
Route-hint pills present on dashboard headers and link to corresponding quick-preview panels
Quick-preview supports metric summary, 7-day sparklines, and cost attribution table; accessible via keyboard and screen reader
Performance: sidebar render and quick-preview open under 120ms on typical production console pages
PM sign-off on discoverability metrics and product analytics for target workflows
implementation_notes: Frontend: Componentized Sidebar with 'mode' prop (global|workspace|contextual); accessibility-first focus management; keyboard shortcuts K to open command palette must still work
Backend: expose workspace configuration API and 'primarySections' ordered list; add feature flag 'ia.layered_sidebar' for gradual rollout
Telemetry: add events for route-hint click, quick-preview open/pin, and deep-link escape hatch time-to-return metrics
risks: Potential regression in existing customers relying on stable left-rail links — mitigated via migration banner and 'classic nav' toggle for 30 days
Increased frontend complexity may introduce bugs in keyboard focus; requires dedicated QA pass and e2e tests
next_steps: Design: finalize responsive states for narrow (<1024px) view and provide collapse behavior
Eng: spike on accessibility focus trap and keyboard nav (ENG-31021)
PM: schedule phased rollout to 10% of tenants behind feature flag and monitor analytics
Schedule: design review 2026-03-09; eng planning 2026-03-12; beta rollout 2026-03-29
